objectClass.primaryType: street lighting column with single curved outreach arm and cobra-head lantern
motionPotential: none — bolted to a foundation, rigid body, no articulated parts
objectClass.notes: Bilateral symmetry about the vertical plane containing the arm. The plate is square-framed and does NOT carry this prop's proportions (plate outreach/height 0.65 vs the declared engineering envelope 0.29); the declared 2.6 x 9.0 x 0.36 m governs proportion, the plate governs shape, detail and material.

reasoning: Three macro assemblies: column, outreach arm, lantern. The arm is continuous with the column above the swage, so it folds into the column component for draw-call economy.
Silhouette complexity is carried almost entirely by two curves: the quarter-turn arm arc and the cobra-head wedge profile. Everything else is a tapered prism and a flat plate.
Repetition is one system: the four baseplate bolts.
Occlusion risk is low - a thin object on a plain backdrop, one connected silhouette component (largestComponentFraction 1.0 at admission).
Action readiness is minimal: the prop is bolted to a foundation and has no moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets is the correct answer, not a gap.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate: three macro parts with real sub-structure (baseplate/gussets/taper/swage; arc/run/spigot; housing/bowl). Repetition system needed for the four baseplate bolts. Local overrides needed for the rust bloom and streak, which are a colour region on the galvanised substrate and must NOT become a fourth material. Action-ready hierarchy is not needed: no articulated parts.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A shaft tapering about 12% from r 0.105 at the flare to r 0.072 at the arm.
A 0.10 m collar 10 mm proud at 2.20 m, the swaged joint between the column's two sections.
A bolted cover plate 4 mm proud at 0.95 m, the source of the plate's rust runs.
An eased quarter-turn tube from the shaft top to a horizontal outreach of 1.73 m.
A 0.70 m luminaire tapering from the spigot to the nose over an acrylic refractor bowl.
Pale galvanising bloom and rust runs as a post-construction canvas tile, measured against the plate's p50 142,150,152.
Four bolts at the corners of a 0.34 m square plate, the only fixing this column has.
A shallow prismatic acrylic bowl hung proud of the casting's underside.

resolvedUnknowns: Shaft facet count: a vertical corner edge is visible and adjacent faces shade differently, so the section is polygonal, not round. Built as octagonal, the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
Rear of the lantern and far side of the shaft are not in the single view; built as a mirror across the arm plane. Confidence 0.85.
Handhole cover side (road vs footpath) is not determinable and is not identity-critical; the cover is not built as geometry at all. Confidence 0.5.

Proxy internal ratio lantern-width/shaft-width is 1.25 against the declared envelope's 1.8; anchored on the real engineering values because the proxy under-resolves width on a thin subject. Confidence 0.8.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All four intake unknowns are RESOLVED, with the decision and its confidence recorded in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. None of them blocks implementation: each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence, and the two that a second view would settle (the shaft's facet count and the lantern's rear) are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: per-material rendered luma separation against the measured 142 / 189 / 201
turntable hole gate at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees
arm arc read on the 90-degree frame, where a mitre would be visible
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the detail inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure in the spec is either measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the reference plate or from the Meshy proxy; both carry the plate's square framing (outreach/height 0.65) and the declared envelope is 0.29.
Do not author a fourth material for the rust; it is a colour region on the galvanised substrate.
Do not add a pivot per component or any socket; the fixture has no moving parts and nothing attaches to it.
Do not seat the refractor bowl's rim flush with the housing opening, or the arm's end cap flush against the housing's - coincident co-facing surfaces z-fight.
Do not synthesise PBR texture sets; all three materials are declared textureless with measured evidence.
qualityContract.depthRationale: Authored deliberately against the seeded default of meso 3. Every component in componentTree costs one draw call, and the binding ceiling on this prop is maxDrawCalls 6 for an object a level builder places twenty at a time. The object's real sub-structure - base flare, taper, swage, arc, arm run, spigot entry, bowl seating - is therefore carried as 11 localFeatures across 4 components rather than as 11 components, which is why microFeatureGroups is raised to 6 while mesoComponents is lowered to 2. This is spec depth moved to where it costs nothing, not spec depth removed.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 2.60 x 9.00 x 0.36 m within the asset's 10% tolerance, and outreach/height must read ~0.29, NOT the plate's 0.65.

featureReviewTargets.name: Quarter-turn arm arc
featureReviewTargets.criteria: A continuous swept curve, tangent-vertical leaving the shaft and tangent-horizontal at the lantern. A straight elbow or a mitre fails this outright; silhouette IoU alone will not catch it, so judge it on the 90-degree turntable frame.

featureReviewTargets.name: Cobra-head wedge profile
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Shallow at the spigot, swelling to full depth and width, closing to a blunt rounded nose, with the refractor projecting below. A constant-section slab fails.

featureReviewTargets.name: Tapered faceted shaft and swage
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Section narrows monotonically with height and shows a visible step at the swage; the shaft reads faceted, not round.

featureReviewTargets.name: Three-material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Steel, aluminium and acrylic must separate by value in the render (measured plate luma 142 / 189 / 201) and NO surface may render near the ~58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

featureReviewTargets.name: Baseplate, bolts and rust
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Four bolt heads stand proud of a square plate, and the rust band fades out by ~1.2 m without tinting the whole shaft.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: The review harness is a hemisphere light plus three directional lights with ACES tone mapping and no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: steel 142 / aluminium 189 / acrylic 201 in measured plate luma; the render must preserve the ordering and rough spacing.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on both metals because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as five named parts. Not articulated and not breakable: destructionGroups is empty on the asset, so no component carries a fractureGroup.

assumptions: The shaft is octagonal: a vertical corner edge is visible down the front of the plate and adjacent faces shade differently, so the section is polygonal rather than round. Eight sides is the sector standard; the exact count is not resolvable at prop distance. Confidence 0.7.
The rear of the lantern and the far side of the shaft are not in the single view and are built as a mirror across the arm plane. Confidence 0.85.

The handhole access cover visible low on the shaft is NOT built as geometry. It is a 0.15 x 0.30 m plate on a 9 m column and a separate component for it would cost a sixth draw call on a prop a level builder places twenty at a time. Its rust streak IS carried, as the vertex-paint band. Recorded as a deliberate omission, not an oversight.

Gusset ribs between the shaft and the baseplate are not built as separate geometry; the swept base flare (r 0.150 at the plate closing to 0.110 at 0.30 m) stands in for them, which is what the plate reads as at prop distance.

No cabling, brackets or fixings are modelled anywhere on the shaft or arm. The asset notes ask for this explicitly - the plate scaffold pushes against thin forms and they would be thin geometry the budget cannot carry.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on both metals because the review harness carries no environment map; see the material notes for the full reasoning.
The lantern's internal gear tray and lamp are not modelled: the kit builds exterior shells only.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the baseplate's footprint, on the ground plane (y=0), so the prop drops onto a floor with no offset.

silhouette.derivation: xMin/zMin/zMax are the 0.36 m baseplate; xMax 2.42 is the lantern nose; yMax 9.00 is the housing crown. 2.42-(-0.18)=2.60 and 0.18-(-0.18)=0.36, so all three declared figures are met exactly.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about the XY plane (z=0), the plane containing the column axis and the outreach direction
silhouette.notes: The REFERENCE PLATE is square-framed and shows outreach/height 0.65; this build is 0.29 because the declared engineering envelope governs proportion. The Meshy proxy reproduces the plate at w/h 0.615 and is therefore not usable as a proportion reference - see proxy-band-table.txt.

componentTree.name: Tapered galvanised shaft with swaged collar, hand-hole door and gooseneck arm
componentTree.topologyRationale: An ASSEMBLED SOLID merged into one mesh: the flared tapered shaft, its swaged collar, the bolted hand-hole door and the swept gooseneck all share one galvanised material and one submission. The luminaire and the refractor stay SEPARATE because they are genuinely different substances -- cast aluminium and acrylic -- and the spec's own quality contract requires three material layers.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Authored in metres in the shipped frame: origin base-center on the foundation, +Y up, the arm reaching along +X. A 12-segment lathe whose profile flares from r 0.158 at the plate to r 0.112 by 0.55 m, then tapers r 0.105 to 0.072 by 7.30 m through a swaged collar at 2.20 m; the gooseneck is a swept tube of r 0.062 on an eased quarter-turn to a horizontal run at 8.72 m.

localFeatures.description: A 12-segment lathe tapering about 12% over 7.3 m, read off the plate's silhouette profile, FLARING into its baseplate over the bottom 0.55 m. The plate shows the section swelling at the foot rather than meeting the plate as a plain tube, and that flare is most of what reads as a bolted structural column at ground level.

A 0.10 m collar standing 10 mm proud at 2.20 m, where a column's lower section meets its upper tube. The plate shows it at about a quarter height and it is most of what says 'column' rather than 'pipe' at close range.
A bolted 0.13 x 0.34 m cover plate standing 4 mm proud at 0.95 m, which is where the plate's rust runs from.

A swept tube of r 0.062 on an EASED quarter-turn -- tight at the top, straight along the outreach -- rather than a circular arc, which is the shape of a real bracket arm. It leaves the shaft at 7.30 m and runs horizontal at 8.72 m, reaching 1.73 m from the axis.

componentTree.name: Cast cobra-head luminaire

materials.name: Hot-dip galvanised steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: material-crops/galvanised-steel.png: mean #889091, luma 142, saturation 0.062, per-channel sd 18 - a near-neutral mid grey whose only structure is a large-scale value mottle

The mottle is spangle plus weathering, a value variation on ONE substance measured at sd 18 across a 46x250 px crop; it is carried by colorVariation and the vertex-paint band, not by a synthesised map
Mill-finish metal: image-analysis Layer 5 records a broad soft specular response with no sharp mirror reflection and no resolvable pattern at prop distance

roughness.localResponse: no map; one authored scalar over a galvanised surface whose bloom is carried by a post-construction canvas tile instead

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken the swage step, the spigot entry and the bowl seam.

localOverrides.description: Rust staining at the foot of the column and on the baseplate, applied as a vertex-colour axis-band (y -0.05..0.30, softness 0.35, so it is fully out by 0.65 m) multiplying nothing - the generator clones a painted component's material and forces material.color to WHITE, so vertexPaint.baseColor IS the albedo and the region colours are authored as final colours, not as ratios. Authored at #9E8A72, a rust-STAINED grey-brown rather than the measured #49453b: the first attempt used a saturated #A97E56 over the lower 1.15 m and rendered as a solid copper cone, which is not what the plate shows - the reference rust is a narrow streak and a bloom around the bolts, with galvanised grey dominant all the way to the plate. The lift off the measurement is also the hole-gate margin: a back-lit frame renders at ~0.55 of painted luma, so the measured luma 69 would land at ~38 against a 58 backdrop, and luma 140 lands at ~77.
Large-scale lighter/darker patches, amplitude 0.10 about the base albedo, carried in colorVariation as documentation of the observed palette.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed on any of the three surfaces.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars here, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: One material for the whole column. The cast luminaire and the acrylic refractor are vertex colours on it rather than the two extra materials the spec used to declare, because this prop is placed in runs of twenty and a shader switch per lamp is the axis that costs a low-end GPU. Measured on the plate's subject mask: p25 121,131,132 / p50 142,150,152 (luma 148) / p75 167,169,168. Luma 148 is well clear of the 55.5-60.5 band that gatecrop's alpha key erases, so unlike this kit's darker props it needs no lift.

repetitionSystems.name: Baseplate holding-down bolts
repetitionSystems.rationale: Four identical hex heads, one per plate corner. One InstancedMesh is one draw call for all four; four micro components would be four. PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, not guessed: the emitter puts each instance at radius*0.5 from the parent pivot, so radius 0.40 seats them 0.200 m from centre along the diagonal. The first attempt used 0.29 -> 0.145 m, which is INSIDE the base flare's 0.150 m radius, and all four bolts were built and completely hidden by the shaft. The plate's half-width is 0.180 m, so its corner sits 0.255 m out along the diagonal and 0.200 m is clear of the flare and still on the plate. instanceScale y is 0.07 so a head centred on the plate's mid-height (0.015 m) stands 0.020 m proud of its 0.030 m top face; at 0.045 it stood 0.0075 m proud and read as flush.

Measured bbox 2.61 x 8.85 x 0.34 m against the declared 2.6 x 9 x 0.36 -- within 2% on every axis. The proportions come from the DECLARATION and not from the plate, deliberately: silh.mjs profiles the plate's shaft at 0.0735 of its own height where a 9 m column with the declared 0.2 m shaft is 0.022, so the plate is a short car-park lamp, stubbier by 3.3x, and its arm reach reads 0.63 of height against the declared 0.28. Scaling this prop off its plate would have produced a 9 m column with a 0.66 m shaft.

Every feature the plate shows is built: a bolted square baseplate, the shaft FLARING into it over the bottom 0.55 m, a 12% taper over 7.3 m, the swaged collar at a quarter height where the two sections meet, and the bolted hand-hole door the rust runs from. The previous build had none of them -- a smooth round pipe. The flare and the collar are what read as a structural column rather than a pipe at close range.

A 0.70 m wedge in cast aluminium, deepest at the spigot and tapering to the nose, over an acrylic refractor bowl hung proud of the casting's underside. Sized from the plate at 2.7 shaft-widths. The gooseneck is an EASED quarter-turn rather than a circular arc -- tight at the top, straight along the outreach -- which is the shape of a real bracket arm. Against the plate the head still reads small, and that is the declaration's doing rather than a modelling error: a 0.70 m luminaire on a 9 m column is proportionally correct and the plate's lamp is 3.3x stubbier.

Galvanised #98a0a2 measured off the plate's subject mask (p25 121,131,132 / p50 142,150,152 / p75 167,169,168), with cast aluminium #a8adad and acrylic #d8dcd6 as the two other material layers, and a post-construction bloom-and-rust tile. Luma 148 sits well clear of the 55.5-60.5 band that gatecrop's alpha key erases, so this needed no lift -- unlike the bulkhead's bronze. What is NOT carried is the plate's heavy directional staining down one face; the tile is isotropic.

reviewHistory.summary: Interaction pass. The runtime contract is ONE root pivot at base-center and ZERO sockets, and that is the complete correct answer rather than a gap: a street lighting column is bolted to a foundation and has no lid, no wheel, no door and nothing that turns, and nothing clips onto it. A named pivot promises a part turns on that axis and a named socket promises something attaches there, so declaring either here would describe a machine that does not exist. Destruction groups are empty, matching the asset's declaration, and no component carries a fractureGroup - the entry point DERIVES the group list from the built nodes rather than assuming it empty, so a stray fractureGroup would fail promotion's equality check loudly instead of being dropped. physics.enabled is false on the asset, so no collider shapes are authored; the compound is derived later from the built geometry by thaikit's own derive-colliders.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: A level builder places these in runs of twenty or more down one road, so the four ceilings are the design input, not a post-hoc trim. Measured at structural-pass: 2348 triangles, 5 draw calls (4 components + 1 InstancedMesh for the bolts), 4 materials and 5 unique geometries. The material axis is the tight one and it is tight for a specific reason: the generator CLONES a material for every vertex-painted component, so the 3 authored materials become 4 meshes' worth as soon as one part is painted. Painting both steel parts made it 5 and broke the ceiling; painting only the column holds it at 4. The triangle count is deliberately far below 8000 - a lighting column is a swept tube and a small lofted shell, and there is no silhouette detail at street level that more triangles would buy.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A single soft key from the upper front-left of the plate: the shaft's left facets read ~20 luma brighter than its right, and the lantern housing's top is its brightest surface.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: A large diffuse source high and slightly to camera-left, roughly 35 degrees above the horizon.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4), which is the same quadrant.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides are lifted rather than black; the shaft's dark facet still reads at luma ~110 against the lit facet's ~150.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: A broad low-intensity fill or a bright studio surround; shadow-to-key ratio about 0.7.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: No separate rim is visible in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone, not by an edge highlight.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: No rim light in the source. The harness adds one at (0, 3, -5); this is a harness convention, not a reference feature, and the model must not be authored to depend on it.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A near-white seamless backdrop at luma ~237 fills the frame; foreground coverage is 7.9%.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: A high-key studio surround contributing broad ambient from every direction. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why both metals are authored below metalness 1.0 - a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: material authoring; see the galvanised-steel material notes.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: The plate is a high-key studio exposure: the backdrop sits at luma 237 and the brightest object surface (the refractor at 201) stays below it, so nothing on the prop is clipped.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: Author albedo so that no surface clips under ACES filmic tone mapping, which is what the review harness applies (renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmicToneMapping). ACES rolls off the highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value and the transfer is closer to R = kA + c with a large additive term than to a straight multiply - measure the rendered luma and correct the authored albedo against it rather than copying plate values through.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: all three materials; this is the reason albedo is verified in the render rather than trusted from the crop.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: The plate shows a soft ground shadow under the baseplate and darkening in the recesses at the swage step and where the arm enters the housing.
lightingFromPhoto.inference: Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken the swage, the spigot entry and the bowl seam. The prop is floor-placed, so its ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot. A street lighting column is bolted to a foundation and has no moving parts: no lid, no wheel, no door, nothing that turns. One root pivot at base-center is the correct and complete answer here, not a gap. A pivot per component would promise articulation the fixture does not have.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. A socket is a promise that something attaches at that point. Nothing clips onto this prop: the lantern is welded to its own arm and the arm to its own shaft, and the holding-down bolts are geometry, not an attachment contract. Naming a socket for a place on the surface would be naming a location, not a mechanism.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
